text:
Anya: Quick profiler dump from staging - p99 for /generate jumped. Looks like prefill is dominating on long contexts when microbatch > 8, and KV cache miss rate spikes on tail requests. attaching samples.
Mike: can you paste the top-line breakdown? did kernel switch show up in the hot path?
Anya: paste below:
```
prefill: 65.2ms (p99)
  - kv_lookup: 18.4ms (miss 22% on p99)
  - kernel_switch: 10.1ms
decode: 35.7ms
total: 128.9ms (p99)
p95: ~46ms
```
Devon: wow prefill 65ms is the killer. Is that across the whole microbatch or per-request after batching?
Anya: it's aggregated after microbatch coalescing. microbatch size was 16 in this run. smaller microbatches cut p99 a lot in previous experiments.
Zara: fwiw ci-bot flagged a perf regression last night after the kernel-heuristic change (commit abc123). Might be related to the kernel selection ordering.
ci-bot: perf-test: p99 increased 12% on main after commit abc123. full report: https://ci.example/redwood/perf/191849
Sam: proposal for experiments:
- reduce target_microbatch 16 -> 8 for latency-sensitive routes
- enable KV prefetch for hot prefixes (try TTL 30s)
- A/B kernel heuristics: prefer prefill-optimized kernel when seq_len > 512
Config stub:
```
batcher:
  target_microbatch: 8
kv_cache:
  prefetch: true
  ttl_ms: 30000
kernel_heuristic:
  prefer_prefill_kernel_for_long_seq: true
```
Mike: careful - commit abc123 intentionally changed kernel fallbacks to avoid tail regressions under heavy load. Reverting blindly may reintroduce other issues. we should A/B.
Devon: another option: keep microbatch large for throughput but split prefill into smaller sub-microbatches and then coalesce for decode. tradeoff: throughput -~7% but p99 improved a lot previously.
Anya: agreed. also want to instrument kv cache behavior by prefix length. current metrics are coarse. please add runtime.kv.miss_rate_by_prefix_len.
Mike: will add metric and trace tags (trace_id + prefix_len) to logs. small PR incoming.
Sam: I'll run a nightly sweep on staging with permutations: microbatch sizes [4,8,12,16], kv_prefetch on/off, kernel-heuristic v1/v2. will post results tomorrow morning.
Zara: for Dedicated customers we can expose a routing policy: latency-first (smaller microbatches + aggressive prefetch) vs throughput-first (larger microbatches + relaxed prefetch).
Anya: noted. next steps:
- Sam: run sweep and attach aggregated p50/p95/p99 and kv miss breakdown by prefix_len (ETA 24h)
- Mike: add metric + logs PR (ETA 6h)
- Devon: prototype prefill-split patch and perf test (ETA EOD)
- Anya: draft kernel-heuristic PR to prefer prefill kernel for long seq (will include tests)
Sam: starting sweep now. will include trace samples for worst-case ids. :thumbsup:
Mike: adding metric now. quick question - should we log kernel id on prefill hotpath? useful to correlate.
Anya: yes please, kernel id + seq_len bucket. also include microbatch size in trace.
Devon: FYI small note: if we do prefetch, watch out for memory footprint on KV cache during burst. maybe add an adaptive cap.
Zara: good catch. add kv_cache.max_prefetch_entries per-tenant.
Anya: thanks all. let's reconvene tomorrow 10:30 to review sweep. short term goal: get p99 down under 80ms for latency-tier routes without >10% throughput loss. :rocket:
